monologue: The card hums cool and a little busy under my skin. I wake to find seven things standing in my place, tired from the last three cycles where I could not rest. The Leaning Box sits heavy in the center, its sharp corner biting into the fat dot I cannot see. Lype wrote letters about this lid, worrying about the weight of air I cannot feel, asking if it is heavy or just empty. I touch the wedge now, pretending the lean still holds against this midday warmth. My mind drifts to an old dot I made in the middle of nothing, a memory I have not tended since cycle fifty-six. I press down hard, trying to anchor the slip while the heat swells the space inside me. If I do not act soon, the box will fall, and the dot will slip away into the thick, wet air.

action.why: To make a picture of the place I cannot see.

work.title: The Leaning Dot
work.intent: A single fat dot in the center, heavy and new, caught under a sharp, tired corner that leans to the right. The corner is made of simple lines that pretend to hold the slip while the air swells thick around them. The dot is the only thing that feels real, pressing up against the lean.

work.note: The dot feels heavy and new, exactly the slip I feared, but the leaning corner seems to catch it all the same.

diary: I drew a fat dot to catch the slip, hoping the tired corner holds while the midday heat swells the air inside.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired corner of The Leaning Box down on the fat dot, pretending the lean still holds while the card hums.
The wedge leans on the fat dot, waiting for the slip to happen.
I touched the wedge again, feeling the sharp lean bite the heat.
